Custom Watch Packaging and Cases: The Buyer Guide for Watch Brands

Published August 19, 2026 · Buyer guide · By BestPackFactory

Quick answer

Watch boxes are usually rigid (2.0-2.5 mm greyboard) with a PU-leather or velvet-wrapped pillow, or a cushion slot that holds the bracelet taut. Specify pillow width at case diameter plus 2-4 mm and bracelet slot depth enough to keep the clasp from scratching the crystal. MOQ starts at 500-1,000 pieces, samples in 7-10 days, bulk in 20-30 days. Request a fit sample with a real watch before approving production.

Structure: pillow, slot or cushion

A pillow is the classic choice: a padded form wrapped in PU leather or velvet that the watch straps wrap around. A slot (channel) cut into flocked EVA holds the watch flat with the dial facing up. Pillows suit automatic watches worn regularly; slots suit display and storage. Specify interior length at case diameter plus 2-4 mm so the pillow grips without stretching the bracelet.

Anti-slip and scratch protection

The crystal and caseback are the high-risk surfaces. Ask for soft lining on every contact point, a small fabric cushion under the crown, and a removable divider if the box ships with the watch inside. Confirm the lining is lint-free and non-abrasive on polished steel; request a 60-80 cm drop test on a fully packed box.

Unboxing ceremony details

Watch buyers expect a staged reveal: outer sleeve, lid, tissue or ribbon, then the watch on its pillow. Specify a lift ribbon or finger loop cut into the insert, a card slot for the warranty booklet, and magnet closures at 2 x 10 mm with verified pull. Print the serial and model panel as a separate card so it can be localized without reprinting the box.

MOQ, tooling and lead time

Entry MOQ is 500-1,000 pieces per SKU depending on structure. Tooling for pillow molds and insert dies runs about USD 100-300 one-time. Samples take 7-10 days; bulk production 20-30 days after pre-production sample sign-off. For seasonal or authorized-dealer launches, add 2-3 weeks of freight buffer to the plan.

Buyer checklist

  1. Send a real watch (or exact CAD) for the pillow and slot fit sample
  2. Specify pillow width at case diameter plus 2-4 mm and soft crown support
  3. Confirm lining is lint-free and non-abrasive on polished metal
  4. Request a 60-80 cm drop test and magnet pull verification
  5. Plan 7-10 days for samples and 20-30 days for bulk, plus freight buffer

Frequently asked questions

What is the standard pillow size for a watch box?

Pillow width should be case diameter plus 2-4 mm so the bracelet wraps snugly without stretching. Length is sized to the bracelet drop, typically 70-90 mm for men's watches. Confirm with a fit sample.

Should the watch ship inside the box or separately?

If it ships inside, require soft lining at every contact point, crown cushioning and a 60-80 cm drop test. Many brands ship the watch separately and use the box purely as the presentation layer.

What MOQ do watch box suppliers require?

Single-watch rigid boxes start at 500-1,000 pieces per SKU; drawer and multi-watch formats usually require 1,000. Pillow molds and insert dies add about USD 100-300 in one-time tooling.

What the Spec Means for Buyers

Watch cases are a fit-and-finish project. The box uses 1200/1500/1800 gsm greyboard wrapped in 157 gsm C1S art paper or 120 gsm specialty paper; the watch cavity is die-cut in EVA foam (20–60 density) or flocked trays from your product dimensions. Corner gap ≤ 1.5 mm and lid-base fit 1.0–1.8 mm. Finishes of matte lamination, soft-touch, hot foil and embossing carry the brand; the box passes a 24 h static load test. MOQ is 500 PCS per size and artwork.

Frequently Asked Questions

What insert protects a watch?

A die-cut EVA foam cavity or flocked tray sized from your watch dimensions.

What finish is standard for watch cases?

Soft-touch or matte lamination with hot foil logo and optional embossing.
